issue: The record has no start/end timestamp field. Plan logic needs 'newest cold full record', 'failing cell from the newest run', and the failed-only 'latest full-scenario record (cold or warm)'. run_id is random hex and job_id holds only HHMM.
implementation_impact: The focus cell and the failed set can't be derived deterministically. Ordering across days or between cold and warm records is guesswork.
suggestion: Add a 'started_at' ISO-8601 UTC field (or 'finished_at') to every record and define 'newest'/'latest' by it, with run_id as the tie-break.

issue: The contract doesn't say how many convergence records a cell keeps. A warm partial run that overwrites a single convergence slot erases the last warm full record that the next failed-only run should read.
implementation_impact: The failed set falls back to a stale cold record or to the full set. Fixed scenarios rerun, or newly failing ones are missed.
suggestion: Define retention: keep the latest convergence record per (cell, scenario_set). Failed-only reads the newest record with scenario_set=full by timestamp.

issue: Deleting or renaming a source file, or copying a file with its old mtime preserved, leaves the newest mtime unchanged. The contract also doesn't say whether tests/e2e specs are part of the fingerprinted source.
implementation_impact: Old evidence stays 'fresh' after a deletion or revert. A full record can also count as full even though a spec was added or removed after it.
suggestion: Fingerprint = hash of the sorted (relpath, size, mtime) list over the module tree including tests/e2e. Any add, delete, or rename changes it.

issue: The field list leaves out authored_assertions, scenario_notes, inconclusive, and browser_notes. Today the aggregate reads these per version to drop ready (smoke-only, skipped specs, authed-BO inconclusive).
implementation_impact: Under 'a missing field is never gate-grade', every new record is non-gate-grade. If those fields are dropped instead, smoke-only and skipped-spec cells can count as passing.
suggestion: Add authored_assertions, scenario_notes, inconclusive, and browser_notes to the per-cell field list. Say that the aggregate applies the existing smoke-only and note gates per cell.

issue: A not-run result never overwrites a record and lives only 'in the run report and aggregate'. The contract doesn't say where it persists, so a later plan can't emit rerun reason 'not-run' after the run report is gone.
implementation_impact: The plan reports 'missing' or 'stale-source' instead of 'not-run'. The CAP-3 reason and the headless not_run_cells can't be rebuilt from records alone.
suggestion: Persist not-run as a separate per-cell marker file (cell, run_id, started_at, reason). The plan reads it only when it is newer than the cell's newest real record.

location: SPEC.md:30 (CAP-3 success); run-phases.md:28 (progress log truncated per run)
issue: A version that fail-fast never starts never truncates its per-version progress log. That log still holds the previous run's bring-up and DONE lines.
implementation_impact: The CAP-3 test 'no bring-up for them' and operator monitoring read stale lines as if they came from this run.
suggestion: When fail-fast skips a cell, truncate or rewrite its progress log with a 'NOT-RUN fail-fast after <ver>:<browser>' line. Otherwise the test filters by run=<run_id>.

issue: A ps-e2e-run.py child drives several engines per version. The contract doesn't say which exit code wins when one engine is conclusive-blocking and another is infra-inconclusive or crashed.
implementation_impact: Fail-fast may not trigger on a real blocking finding, or it triggers on the wrong code, depending on how the codes are combined.
suggestion: State the precedence: conclusive-blocking exit wins over exit 1 whenever any engine in the child produced a conclusive blocking finding. Exit 2 stays highest.

location: cell-contract.md:99 (concurrent BO login test, sequential fallback)
issue: The sequential fallback is defined by a test result per version, not by a runtime check. If a parallel BO login fails at runtime, nothing falls back.
implementation_impact: One engine gets bo_authed=false, so the cell is inconclusive and blocks promotion on every retry instead of falling back to sequential.
suggestion: At runtime, if either engine's _bo_login fails while the other engine is logged in, rerun that engine sequentially after the other finishes, and log the fallback.

issue: The contract doesn't define the lock mechanism, a wait timeout, or what happens when the holder crashes or hangs. The browser phase has no timeout, so one hung BO scenario blocks the other engine indefinitely.
implementation_impact: A crashed or hung child can deadlock the version's other engine, and the run never reaches DONE.
suggestion: Use an OS file lock (flock on <run-tmp>/<container>.bo.lock), which is released when the holder process dies. Set a lock-wait timeout that marks waiting scenarios inconclusive and logs SLOW.

issue: The lock covers one BO scenario at a time. It does not cover FO-only scenarios that read BO-mutated state, or the gap between a prerequisite and its dependent on the same engine.
implementation_impact: The other engine's BO scenario can change shared config between bo-setup-country and checkout-with-bank. The 'findings identical to sequential' claim then fails nondeterministically.
suggestion: Hold the lock across a whole requires chain that contains a BO step, or take a shared/read lock for FO scenarios that list a BO scenario in their transitive requires.

issue: The contract doesn't say what a run does when a prerequisite scenario fails or is inconclusive at runtime: run the dependent anyway, skip it, or mark it inconclusive.
implementation_impact: Dependents report cascading failures as their own. The failed-only set then grows with false failures attributed to the wrong scenario.
suggestion: If any transitive prerequisite is not ok in this run, mark the dependent inconclusive with reason 'prerequisite <name> failed' and don't count it as a blocking finding.

location: cell-contract.md:85-86,91 (failed set keyed by name; requires by name)
issue: Two spec files can share a 'name', or one spec's name can equal another file's stem. Neither requires resolution nor the failed-set lookup handles duplicates.
implementation_impact: The rerun drives the wrong spec or both specs, and a requires edge points at an ambiguous target.
suggestion: In discover_scenarios, skip every spec whose effective name collides with another spec's, and write a note naming both files.

location: cell-contract.md:85-86 (failed set; name not matching a spec -> full set)
issue: The universal smoke ('psm-universal-smoke') is builtin and has no spec file. If the smoke failed, the failed set holds a name that matches no spec.
implementation_impact: Any smoke failure silently turns every failed-only rerun into a full run.
suggestion: Exempt the builtin smoke name from the no-match check. The smoke always runs in a failed-only rerun anyway.

location: cell-contract.md:78 (warm reset: restore baseline captured before first install)
issue: Restoring a mysqldump taken before install does not drop tables the module created later. The dump has DROP TABLE only for tables that existed when it was taken.
implementation_impact: Module tables and rows from iteration N survive into N+1 (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS keeps them). This breaks the CAP-5 'DB row absent' test and the reset guarantee.
suggestion: Before the restore, drop every table not in the baseline's table list, or restore into a recreated database (DROP DATABASE; CREATE DATABASE; load dump).

issue: The reset removes only modules/<mod>, overrides, and var/cache. Files the module or its scenarios write elsewhere (themes/*/modules/<mod>, img/, upload/, translations/, mails/) persist. Also, a CLI opcache_reset does not clear the web SAPI's opcache.
implementation_impact: Leftover files or cached bytecode from iteration N cause or hide findings in N+1.
suggestion: Snapshot the docroot file list at baseline and delete any file added afterwards. Reset opcache through the web SAPI (an HTTP endpoint or php-fpm/apache reload).

issue: The contract doesn't say when the idle clock starts or whether an attached iteration counts as activity. An iteration running longer than the TTL, or an attach that arrives just as the TTL expires, can race the teardown.
implementation_impact: The keeper tears down the container mid-iteration, and the iteration becomes inconclusive for an unrelated reason.
suggestion: The keeper counts an attached iteration as active (attach/detach lease file). The idle clock starts at detach, and teardown runs only under the lease lock when no attach is held.

issue: Nothing stops two iterations, from two sessions or two orchestrator calls, from attaching to the same warm container at once.
implementation_impact: Concurrent DB restore, module copy, and browser runs corrupt each other's state and evidence.
suggestion: Make attach take an exclusive lease from the keeper. A second --use-warm gets busy, then either waits or cold-boots, and logs the reason.

location: cell-contract.md:73-75; tier-matrix.md:14 (warm Job ID across iterations)
issue: The contract doesn't say where the warm Job ID is persisted between iterations, so a later iteration or a new session can find it for --use-warm. The plan derives from records only.
implementation_impact: When the ID is lost, a second keeper boots for the same cell. The orphaned keeper holds a slot for up to the TTL.
suggestion: Find the warm keeper through the job registry by (module, version, browser, layer=e2e-warm). --keep-warm refuses to start a second keeper for the same module and version.

issue: The live keeper's slot is counted before admission, but the contract doesn't say whether that counts against the iteration that attaches to it.
implementation_impact: With psm_e2e_slots=1 and a live keeper, the warm iteration can never be admitted, which is a deadlock.
suggestion: An attaching iteration uses its keeper's slot. Admission subtracts that keeper from the count for --use-warm runs.

issue: The contract doesn't say whether the cap is per invocation or host-wide: other sessions' cold runs, or only keepers? It also doesn't say what happens when no slot is free: wait, fail, or a timeout and exit code.
implementation_impact: Parallel sessions together exceed the cap on the shared daemon, or a run blocks with no logged reason.
suggestion: Count all live e2e job registry entries host-wide by slot cost. When the cap is full, wait and emit ALIVE 'waiting-slots' lines, with a bounded timeout that leads to an inconclusive result.

issue: A non-integer psm_e2e_slots, and a zero, negative, or non-integer psm_e2e_warm_ttl, have no defined handling. Only slots < 1 is covered.
implementation_impact: The behavior is undefined. For example, TTL=0 tears down immediately, and a non-integer value crashes the parse.
suggestion: Make any non-integer slots or TTL < 1 an input error (exit 2), the same as slots < 1.

issue: The contract doesn't say how plan, aggregate, and runner normalize psm_target_versions and psm_e2e_browsers (dedup, unsupported engine, empty value). The runner's parse_browsers drops unknown engines and defaults an empty value, and 'newest' has no defined version ordering.
implementation_impact: Plan and aggregate can require a cell the runner never drives, or an empty set makes E2E ready vacuously true. A lexical sort makes '10.0' older than '9.1'.
suggestion: Use one shared normalizer: dedup, reject an unsupported engine or an empty set with exit 2, and sort versions semantically. Plan, aggregate, and runner all import it.

issue: 'Failing' is computed from records without filtering to configured cells. A stale fail record for a version or browser that was later removed from config can still become the focus cell.
implementation_impact: The loop focuses on a cell that is not configured and never leaves loop-back.
suggestion: Restrict failing and focus derivation to the current configured cells, and ignore records outside them.

issue: The orchestrator 'runs exactly e2e_next_cells'. Nothing says what happens when the interactive scope menu or headless arguments exclude those cells, such as the canary or the focus cell.
implementation_impact: The orchestrator either breaks the narrowing or never makes tier progress. Behavior differs between implementations.
suggestion: Have the plan take the narrowed scope: e2e_next_cells = plan cells ∩ scope. If that is empty, emit e2e_step 'blocked-by-scope' and report it.

issue: The per-version mapping covers not-run, partial, warm-only, and inconclusive. It misses versions whose cells are missing or stale because headless stopped before tier 1, and it has no precedence when a version has both a failing cell and a not-run cell.
implementation_impact: Callers get an undefined or inconsistent per-version verdict for versions that were never tested.
suggestion: Missing or stale map to inconclusive with reason 'tier not reached'. Any conclusive fail makes the version fail, and inconclusive applies only when nothing failed.

location: tier-matrix.md:19; SPEC.md:52 (Layer 3 spawned at Phase 2 start, concurrent with tier 1)
issue: A blocking finding from Layer 3, 2, or 5 in Phase 2 forces a source patch while tier 1 cells are in flight. Nothing stops in-flight or queued tier 1 cells, which are already stale.
implementation_impact: Hours of cold boots produce evidence that is stale on arrival, and the plan has to re-derive the step without being told.
suggestion: When the source fingerprint changes mid-gate, ps-run-layer stops admitting queued cells and records them as not-run with reason 'source changed'.

location: cell-contract.md:105-107 (phase timings in a CAP-7 pair)
issue: Boot phases (pull through warmup-bo, plus teardown) are shared by both cells of one boot. The contract doesn't say whether each cell record copies them, or whether wall_clock is per engine or per boot.
implementation_impact: e2e_phase_durations double-counts boot time, or attributes it to one browser only, which skews the boot-versus-browser comparison.
suggestion: Tag shared phases with a boot_id and store them once per boot. Per-cell records hold only browser:<engine> plus a reference to boot_id. wall_clock stays per cell from engine start to end.
